title: Flagrant Denial of Justice: The Systematic Elimination of Law
subtitle: Where justice is replaced by bureaucratic paralysis. In the Lagovsky case, the Russian legal system has demonstrated its utter inability to provide even the minimum standard required by Article 6 ECHR.
intro: More than 15 official petitions to the supervisory and judicial bodies of the Russian Federation have led to a single outcome: a total refusal to examine the merits of the defense's arguments. This is not a series of isolated errors, but a documented systemic 'flagrant denial of justice'. Under ECtHR and UN standards, such a pattern acts as an absolute bar to extradition, as surrender to a system stripped of protective mechanisms is in itself a violation of the extraditing state's international obligations.

un_block.title: UN Standards: The Immunity of Legal Professionalism
un_block.intro: The UN Basic Principles on the Role of Lawyers (Havana, 1990) establish a global standard for protecting lawyers from arbitrary prosecution. Russia, as a UN member, systematically ignores these imperatives in the Lagovsky case.
un_block.url_label: UN Basic Principles on the Role of Lawyers (ohchr.org)

principles.text: Access to a lawyer and protection at all stages of criminal proceedings.
principles.relevance: Lagovsky is stripped of this right: his complaints are rejected by courts based on his status as 'wanted,' creating a legally insurmountable barrier to challenging the indictment.

principles.text: Freedom from intimidation and improper interference.
principles.relevance: The initiation of criminal proceedings against a lawyer for fulfilling the terms of a commercial contract is a classic example of improper interference with professional functions.

principles.text: Prohibition of identifying a lawyer with their client.
principles.relevance: The investigation attributes the actions of the client to the lawyer, directly violating the international standard of legal professional independence.

principles.text: Right to freedom of expression and participation in discussions on the law.
principles.relevance: Blocking access to the court deprives Lagovsky of the only lawful way to professionally and personally express his position on the case.

echr_block.title: ECtHR Precedent: The Threshold for Refusing Surrender

paras.text: In Othman (Abu Qatada) v. UK (2012), the Court held: extradition is impermissible if there is a real risk of a 'flagrant denial of justice.' This is a situation where the breach is so fundamental as to destroy the very essence of the fair trial guarantee.

Golder v. UK (1975) established that the right of access to a court is not a mere formality but the core of Article 6 ECHR. A system that uses criminal prosecution as a pretext to strip away the right to appeal violates the very nature of justice.

In Kudła v. Poland (2000), the ECtHR emphasized: legal remedies must be 'effective in practice,' not just on paper. Formulaic 'cut-and-paste' responses and the circular collusion of the prosecution are direct evidence of the absence of such remedies.

pattern_title: The Mechanics of Refusal: Systemic Collusion
pattern_desc: Documentary analysis of the official responses reveals a stable pattern: complaints are forwarded to the very persons against whom they are filed, and courts use the defendant's status as a shield against his own petitions. This is a circular paralysis of law.

docs_cta.title: Evidence of Systemic Failure
docs_cta.desc: A collection of official responses confirming the impossibility of protecting rights within the Russian Federation.

episodes.title: Moscow Region Prosecutor: The Erosion of Oversight
episodes.what_happened: The Moscow Region Prosecutor's Office built a wall of eight identical template refusals. Instead of verifying arguments regarding the res judicata effect of arbitration rulings, the supervisory body limited itself to the phrase 'no violations established,' effectively delegating the oversight function to the investigators themselves. This turns prosecutorial supervision into mere window-dressing.
episodes.quote: "Procedural decisions have been reviewed... as you have been previously notified on multiple occasions."
episodes.why_flagrant: A violation of Article 13 ECHR. The absence of an independent and effective remedy makes extradition impossible, as it deprives the accused of any chance to challenge arbitrary acts before the case reaches trial.
violations: Violation of the principle of independent prosecutorial oversight

un_refs_html: UN Basic Principles on the Role of Lawyers, Principle 16

episodes.title: General Prosecutor's Office: Legitimatizing Arbitrariness
episodes.what_happened: The General Prosecutor's Office of the Russian Federation ignored the fundamental conflict between arbitration and criminal law in five separate responses. Furthermore, in a response dated March 17, 2026, the body cited the convictions of third parties as evidence of Lagovsky's guilt, a gross violation of the presumption of innocence by the highest supervisory authority.
episodes.quote: "There are currently no grounds for the intervention of the GPO RF."
episodes.why_flagrant: A direct violation of Article 6 §2 ECHR. Using the convictions of others to pre-judge the guilt of a person not involved in those proceedings demonstrates the pervasive bias of the entire prosecutorial system.
violations: Art. 18 ECHR (Political Motives for Restricting Rights)
echr_refs_html: Mamatkulov and Askarov v. Turkey (2005)
un_refs_html: UN Basic Principles on the Role of Lawyers, Principle 18

episodes.title: Moscow City Court: Judicial Segregation
episodes.what_happened: The Moscow City Court officially refused to consider a petition, citing the 'impossibility of identifying the wanted person.' This creates a legal paradox: a person is deprived of the right to judicial protection precisely because they need protection from an arbitrary warrant. This is not law; it is the liquidation of legal personhood before the state.
episodes.quote: "Due to the impossibility of identifying the applicant... the petition is left without consideration."
episodes.why_flagrant: A classic flagrant denial under Golder. Depriving access to a court based on the formal status of being 'wanted' makes any fair trial in the future impossible.
violations: Art. 6 §1 ECHR (Right of Access to Court)

conclusion_paras: The facts presented confirm the existence of a persistent practice of procedural sabotage in the Russian Federation. When none of the three levels of oversight (regional, federal, judicial) examines defense arguments on their merits, the right to a fair trial ceases to exist even as a theoretical possibility.

In accordance with the international principle of non-refoulement and the standards set by Othman v. UK, surrendering Lagovsky to a jurisdiction where access to justice is blocked would constitute a direct violation of Serbia's obligations under the ECHR. Flagrant denial of justice is not a hypothetical threat but a documented fact established by the responses of the prosecution and the courts.

As human rights advocates and international lawyers, we state: in this case, the extradition request is legally void, as its fulfillment would lead to an irreversible violation of fundamental human rights.
summary: Russia has de facto abolished the institution of judicial protection for Dmitry Lagovsky. The systemic refusals of the prosecution and courts to examine complaints on their merits constitute a classic 'flagrant denial of justice'. According to ECtHR precedents (Othman, Golder, Kudła), this provides an absolute ground for refusing extradition.
